MEASUREMENT.VERDICT_REASON: Source identity, compile, link, correctness, and same-binary all PASS. The paired measurement on the exercising shape (D=32768) shows a stable improvement: 8/8 blocks negative across two independent devices, median -3.66%, range -4.72% to -3.00%, all blocks clean (MAD <= 0.027). The improvement is well outside the measured noise band (about plus or minus 1% from the same-code D=24576 control). Hoisting the invRms row-scale Muls out of the per-tile affine loop removes one full-tile V pass and one PipeBarrier per tile (5 tiles at D=32768), and the effect is larger than the predicted 0.4 us: observed about 0.7 us (parent 19.0 us -> candidate 18.3 us), consistent with barrier removal unblocking the V pipeline more than the per-barrier estimate.
MEASUREMENT.MECHANISM_READ: The per-tile Muls and its PipeBarrier serialized the value path five times per row at D=32768. Collapsing them into one full-row Muls before the loop removes four V instruction issues and four PipeBarriers from the critical path. The observed ~3.5% (about 0.7 us of a 19 us kernel) exceeds the naive 5 x 0.08 us = 0.4 us barrier-cost estimate, indicating each per-tile barrier carried more pipeline-stall cost than assumed. The arithmetic is bit-identical to V016 (correctness max_abs matches exactly), so the gain is purely from reduced V-issue and barrier overhead.
